title: Efficient DETR: Improving End-to-End Object Detector with Dense Prior

problem.summary: The paper argues that end-to-end transformer detectors like DETR and Deformable DETR only work well because they stack 6 decoder layers in a cascade, and that the real cause is the random initialization of object containers (object queries and reference points); this makes training slow (10-20x more epochs than mainstream detectors) while dense anchor-based detectors still depend on hand-crafted NMS to be usable.
statements: DETR-style end-to-end detectors rely on a cascade of 6 decoder layers to update object queries iteratively, and performance degrades seriously without it.
Random initialization of object containers (object queries and reference points) is mainly responsible for the requirement of multiple iterations.
DETR requires 10 to 20 times the training epochs of modern mainstream detectors to converge.
Removing decoder iterations is costly: a 1-layer decoder loses 10.3 AP relative to a 6-layer decoder.

evidence.quote: The recently proposed end-to-end transformer detectors, such as DETR and Deformable DETR, have a cascade structure of stacking 6 decoder layers to update object queries iteratively, without which their performance degrades seriously.
we investigate that the random initialization of object containers, which include object queries and reference points, is mainly responsible for the requirement of multiple iterations.
However, DETR requires 10 to 20 times of training epochs than modern mainstream detectors [27, 24, 20] to converge
There is a huge drop of 10.3 AP between a 6-layer decoder and a 1-layer decoder. It is worth noting that only object queries are updated after each iteration.

background.summary: The work builds on DETR's bipartite-matching set prediction, Deformable DETR's fast-converging sparse attention, and Sparse R-CNN's sparse proposals, while contrasting them with dense sliding-window detectors that need NMS; the claimed gap is that no prior end-to-end detector has a good initial state for its object containers.

relatedWork.name: DETR
relatedWork.relation: prior end-to-end set-prediction detector with bipartite matching, but very slow to converge
relatedWork.quote: Recently, DETR [2] proposed to build an end-to-end framework based on an encoder-decoder transformer [34] architecture and bipartite matching, which directly predicts a set of bounding boxes without post-processing.

relatedWork.name: Deformable DETR
relatedWork.relation: prior work that speeds convergence with local attention and multi-scale feature maps
relatedWork.quote: Deformable DETR [43] solves the two problems in the following two aspects: (i). replacing global scoped attention with local spatial attention, which accelerates the convergence of training.

relatedWork.name: Sparse R-CNN
relatedWork.relation: sparse-proposal detector with learnable proposals that converges in 36 epochs
relatedWork.quote: The RoI layer limits the proposal feature to only interact with a few local features and makes Sparse RCNN have a fast converging speed (36 epochs).

relatedWork.name: Modern anchor-based detectors
relatedWork.relation: dense sliding-window detectors whose NMS post-processing prevents end-to-end detection
relatedWork.quote: Modern detectors [9, 27, 24, 20] generate dense anchors with the sliding window method to establish connections between network predictions and the ground truth. Post-processing methods like non-maximum suppression (NMS) is used to remove the redundancy of predictions.

evidence.quote: End-to-end detectors, such as [36], DETR [2], Deformable DETR [43], and Sparse RCNN [31], don't require extra post-processing stages and perform object detection in an end-to-end framework.

However, object queries are randomly initialized at the start of training. We hypothesize that this random initialization does not offer a good initial state, which might be the reason why DETR needs a cascade structure of 6 iterations to achieve competitive performance.

solution.summary: Efficient DETR adds a dense prior to set prediction: a class-specific sliding-window head produces proposals, and the top-K (K=100) scored 4-d proposals with their 256-d encoder features become the reference points and object queries of a 3-encoder, 1-decoder transformer, which refines them with one-to-one Hungarian assignment instead of a 6-layer decoder cascade.
solution.approach: Initialize object queries and reference points from top-K dense sliding-window proposals (dense prior) so that a single decoder layer with one-to-one Hungarian matching suffices, eliminating both the cascade and NMS.
components: Dense part: class-specific sliding-window prediction generating candidate proposals, sharing the detection head with the sparse part
Top-K (K=100) selection of 4-d proposals and their 256-d features as reference points and object queries
3 encoder layers and only 1 decoder layer, without the 6-layer cascade structure
Dynamically tuned proposal number: starts at 300 and decreases linearly to 100 during training
One-to-one label assignment via the Hungarian algorithm shared by dense and sparse parts

evidence.quote: we present a simple but efficient framework for object detection, called Efficient DETR. It has 3 encoder layers and only 1 decoder layer, without the cascade structure in the decoder.

In the dense part, a class specific dense prediction based on sliding-windows is performed to generate proposals. Top-K (K=100 in this paper) scored 4-d proposals and their 256-d encoder features are taken as the reference points and object queries.

In the sparse part, object containers, the reference points, and object queries initialized with dense prior are fed to a 1-layer decoder to interact with the encoder feature for further refinement. The final results are predicted from the refined object containers.
To avoid post-processing like NMS, a one-to-one label assignment rule is adopted. Following [30, 2, 43], we match predictions with ground truth by Hungarian algorithm [16].

experiments.summary: The paper evaluates on COCO 2017 (train2017/val2017) against modern one-stage, two-stage and end-to-end detectors with ResNet-50/101 backbones over 36-epoch schedules, and on CrowdHuman for crowded scenes, plus ablations on decoder stacking, proposal numbers, head sharing and label assignment.

benchmarks.split: same schedule contrasted with DETR's 500 epochs

evidence.quote: our Efficient DETR based on ResNet50 achieves 44.2 AP with 36 epochs training, outperforming Faster RCNN and most end-to-end detectors with fewer FLOPs and parameters.
It achieves the-state-of-the-art in 45.2 AP, with a 6-encoder and 1-decoder structure, which still has fewer parameters than other end-to-end models, thanks to the reasonable design of its framework.
Efficient DETR outperforms other detectors by a large margin, e.g., 4 AP and 5 mMR gains over the Deformable DETR. Especially, our approach achieves this with only 100 proposals.

limitations.summary: Even with a fast 36-epoch schedule, Efficient DETR still trails the state-of-the-art Sparse R-CNN by 0.3 AP on COCO, and its dense-proposal design can introduce extra false positives when many proposals are used in crowded scenes; adding decoder layers on top of it does not help.
items: 0.3 AP below Sparse R-CNN on COCO 2017 val (44.2 vs 44.5) for the 3-encoder, 1-decoder ResNet-50 model.
A large number of proposals may bring more false positives to the final results, especially in crowded scenes.
Cascading decoder layers after Efficient DETR brings only slight improvement and degrades performance after two iterations.

evidence.quote: is only a 0.3 drop in AP (44.2 AP vs 44.5 AP) compared to the state-of-the-art Sparse RCNN.
A large number of proposals may bring more false positives to the final results.

stacking decoder layers after Efficient DETR brings slight improvement. Instead, the model's performance even degrades after two iterations. It indicates that cascading decoder layers to Efficient DETR is not necessary.

futureDirections.direction: Use the dense-prior design as inspiration for simpler, more efficient end-to-end object detectors.
futureDirections.quote: We hope our work could inspire designs of more simple and efficient object detectors.

deploymentClaims: 44.2 AP with 36 epochs of training, a 10 times faster convergence speed than the original DETR (36 epochs vs 500 epochs).
Only 20 percent fewer parameters than most models (32M vs 40M), and it only needs a small number of 100 proposals to achieve this performance.

evidence.quote: It has a 10 times faster convergence speed than the original DETR (36 epochs vs 500 epochs). On the other hand, Efficient DETR outperforms Deformable DETR by 0.4 AP with a simpler structure (3-encoder and 1-decoder vs 6-encoder and 6-decoder) and fewer training epochs (36epochs vs 50 epochs).
